- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect market resilience.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day until trend reverses.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; use 14-day rolling average of price + sentiment to anchor long-term expectation.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +0.5, -0.5, +0.5), model often misaligns with sentiment; weight sentiment more heavily in early forecast periods.
